text:
I don't really know where to start, so I'll just tell you everything. I'm 31 and I work as a data engineer in Pune. About two months ago my company offered me a transfer to their Toronto office. It's a big step up, double the salary in real terms, and honestly it's the kind of opportunity I've worked towards for eight years. My manager says if I turn it down, it won't come again for a long time.

The problem is my parents. My father had a stroke last year and he can walk now but only slowly, and my mother has diabetes and bad knees. They live in Nagpur, about twelve hours from me, and I go every few weeks and handle all their hospital visits, the bills, the insurance, everything. They depend on me for almost everything practical. My younger brother lives in Nagpur, literally twenty minutes from them, but he isn't stepping up. He says he's busy with his own family and his shop, and when I ask him to take Papa to the physiotherapist he says yes and then doesn't go. Last month Papa missed two sessions because of that.

My wife wants us to go. She says we have been putting our lives on hold and that if we don't go now we never will. She also says it's not fair that I carry everything while my brother does nothing. My mother hasn't said don't go, but she cried on the phone when I told her, and then said 'do what is right for you, beta', which somehow made it worse.

I feel guilty when I think about leaving and resentful when I think about staying. I keep thinking, if something happens to Papa while I'm in Canada, I will never forgive myself. But I also don't want to be forty and bitter. My company needs an answer in three weeks. My phone screen cracked last week too, which is a small thing, but everything feels like too much right now. What should I do?

I've been at my job in an accounts department for six years. I'm the person everyone dumps work on. When someone in the team doesn't finish their reconciliation, it lands on my desk at 5:30 with a 'you're so good at this'. Two colleagues in particular, Ravi and Sunita, take credit in meetings for analysis I did, and when I raised it once with our team lead, he laughed and said I should be a team player. Last quarter I stayed late 41 evenings. I counted.

The thing is, I can't just quit. I'm the family's main earner. My husband lost his job in March and is doing some freelance work but it's irregular. We have two kids, 9 and 12, school fees, and the EMI on our flat. My mother-in-law lives with us and her medicines alone are almost eight thousand a month. If I lose this salary even for two months, we are in serious trouble.

I have started dreading Sunday evenings. I snap at the kids, which I hate. My husband says just ignore them at work, keep your head down, it's only a job. But it's not only a job, it's most of my waking hours, and I feel invisible and used. I've thought about looking for another job, but every time I open the job sites I feel tired before I start, and interviews mean taking leave I can't easily get.

My friend says I should go to HR, but HR is the team lead's cousin, and I'm scared of being labelled difficult before appraisals. Part of me thinks maybe this is just what work is, and I'm being too sensitive. Another part of me is angry, really angry, and I don't like who I'm becoming. I want to protect my family and I also want some self-respect back. Is there a way to do both?

My parents want me to marry someone of their choosing. I'm 27, a doctor doing my residency in Hyderabad, and for the past two years I have been seeing someone else. His name is Arjun, he's a teacher, kind, steady, and from a different community. My parents don't know about him. They have been 'showing me profiles' for a year, and now they have found a family they really like, a cardiologist's son, and they want us to meet next month 'just to talk'.

My father is a proud man and he has always said that our family's name matters more than anything. When my cousin married outside the community, he stopped speaking to her family for five years. My mother is softer but she follows him. They sacrificed a lot for my education, loans, my father worked double shifts, and I know they see my marriage as the last thing they need to see done well.

Arjun has been patient but he says he can't wait forever, and that if I'm not going to tell my parents, he needs to know. He's right. I love him and I can't imagine marrying someone else. But I also can't imagine losing my parents, or being the reason my father is humiliated in front of our relatives. My younger sister says she will support me whatever I decide, but she still lives at home and I don't want her to pay for my choice.

I keep delaying. Every week I tell myself I'll talk to them on Sunday, and every Sunday I don't. I'm sleeping badly and I cried in the hospital washroom yesterday, which I've never done. I don't want to choose between love and family. I want to know if there's a way to tell them that gives us the best chance, and what I do if they say no.

My mother has dementia, diagnosed three years ago, and she has lived with us since my father died. I'm 52, a school administrator, and my wife and I have been married twenty-four years. In the beginning Amma just forgot names. Now she wanders at night, sometimes doesn't know who I am, and last week she left the gas on. We have a day carer five days a week but nights are ours, and my wife, Lakshmi, is the one who gets up most nights because I have to be at work at seven.

Lakshmi is exhausted. She has started saying that we need to move Amma to a care home, there is a good one about forty minutes away with a dementia unit. She says it isn't safe anymore and that our marriage is falling apart, and she's right that we barely talk except about medicines and schedules. Our son is in college and avoids coming home.

I am the only son. In our family, the son looks after his parents, full stop. When my uncle heard us mention a care home he said 'is this how you repay her?' and I haven't been able to stop hearing that. When Amma has a good day and calls me by my childhood name, I feel I could never send her away. On bad days I feel like a stranger in my own house.

The care home costs a lot, but we can manage it if we sell a plot of land my father left. My sister lives abroad and sends money sometimes but says it's my decision since I'm here. I don't know if moving her would be giving up on her or protecting her, and I don't know if staying as we are is duty or just my fear of what people will say. What is the right thing here?

ok so basically my dad has this textile business in Surat that his father started and it's been going down for like three years now and last month he called me and said beta I can't do this anymore I need you to come and take over and I'm a nurse I work in the ICU in Bangalore and I love it I really love it like it's the one thing I'm sure about in my life and he knows that but he says a nursing job is a job and this is our family's name and forty people work there and if it closes they all lose their jobs and some of them have been with us since before I was born like Kishore uncle who basically raised me when my parents were busy and I feel sick thinking about him losing his job but I also know nothing about textiles honestly I'd probably run it into the ground faster and my mom is saying don't put pressure on her but also she keeps sending me photos of the shop and old family pictures which is pressure honestly and my boyfriend says I should stay in nursing because I'd be miserable but he's not the one who has to face my dad and I'm thirty and I'm the only child so there's no one else and my dad has blood pressure issues and the doctor said stress is bad for him and I keep thinking what if something happens to him and I said no and the business closed I don't know I just feel like whatever I choose I'm letting someone down and I don't even know what questions I should be asking and the other thing is my dad never asked me before what I wanted he always said do whatever makes you happy and now suddenly it's about the family name and I don't know if he's scared or if he really thinks I'm the right person and when I was little I used to sit in the shop on Saturdays and count the bundles of cloth with Kishore uncle and I loved that too so it's not like I hate it I just don't think I'm the person to save it

My father passed away last year and in his will he made me the executor. There is the ancestral house in our village in Kerala, where we all grew up, and some savings. My elder sister wants to sell the house. She says nobody lives there, it's falling apart, the roof leaks every monsoon, and the money would help her son's education abroad. My mother wants to keep it. She lives with me in Kochi now but she goes back for every festival and says it's where my father is, where his things are. She says selling it would be like selling him.

My younger brother doesn't care either way, he just wants his share, and he's been calling me every week asking when it'll be settled. He has debts I'm not supposed to know about. As executor, I'm supposed to be fair, but I don't think fair means the same thing to all of them.

I have my own feelings too. I'm 44, I have two daughters, and part of me wanted to keep the house for them, so they know where they come from. But I can't afford to buy out my siblings and also repair it. The repairs alone are estimated at eight lakhs.

Last week my sister said if I don't agree to sell, she'll take it to court. My mother heard and didn't eat that evening. I hate that this has become about money when my father would have wanted us to stay close. I want to do my duty as executor properly, keep the family together and respect my mother, and I don't see how to do all three. Where do I start?

When we were children, all three of us used to sleep on the verandah of that house in the summer, and my father would tell us stories about his own father. My sister and I were very close then. Now we only talk through messages, and every message is about valuations and lawyers. I feel I am losing my sister over a house that is supposed to remind us we are one family. My wife says I am too soft and that I should simply follow the law. But the law does not tell me how to look my mother in the eye.

My husband has a gambling problem. I found out properly in January when the bank called about a loan I didn't know existed. It started with online rummy during the lockdown and now it's sports betting. He's lost around six lakhs that I know of. He's not violent, I want to say that clearly, he's a gentle person, and when I confronted him he cried and promised to stop. He stopped for three weeks. Then I found the app again.

We have two children, 7 and 10. They adore him. My salary as a bank clerk covers the house and fees but not the loan repayments, and I've started taking money from my provident fund. My parents don't know. If they knew they would tell me to come home, and I'm not sure I want that.

I've been reading about separation, but then I think about the kids and how much they love their father, and about what people will say, and about whether I'm giving up on him when he's sick. Because I do think it's an illness. But I also feel like I'm drowning. I lie awake every night doing calculations. Some nights I feel hopeless, like nothing I do will fix this.

He says he'll go to a counsellor but he hasn't booked anything. I don't know whether to stay and help him get better, or protect the children and myself by separating our finances or even separating completely. I don't want my children to grow up with this, and I don't want them to grow up without their father either.

I keep a notebook now with every rupee. I hide the cards. I check his phone when he sleeps, which makes me feel like someone I don't recognise. My closest friend from work knows a little, and she says I should talk to a lawyer just to understand my options, even if I don't use them. My daughter asked me last week why I always look tired. I told her it's work. I am so tired of lying to everyone, including myself. Some days I think if I just try harder, plan better, watch him more closely, I can hold it all together.

I'm an engineer at a construction firm in Dubai, on an employment visa that depends on this job. Three months ago I noticed that my manager was signing off on concrete test reports that I know are wrong. I ran the tests myself on two batches and they failed strength requirements, but the reports he submitted say they passed. The building is a residential tower, twenty-two floors, families will live there.

When I mentioned it to him privately, he said the lab made errors and the margin is fine, and that I should focus on my own work. A week later I was moved off that project. My colleague who also saw the results told me to keep quiet, that people who make trouble here get sent home.

I have a wife and a baby daughter here, and we send money every month to my parents in Kerala, who have a loan on their house that I'm paying. If I lose this job, I lose the visa within thirty days and the whole family has to go back. I've thought about reporting it to the municipality or the developer, but I don't know if it would be anonymous. I've also thought about just finding another job first and then reporting it, but that could take months and they're already pouring the upper floors.

I can't sleep thinking about a building coming down. I also can't sleep thinking about my daughter's future. My father always told me to be honest even when it costs you. I don't know if he understood how much it can cost. What should I do?

I have saved some emails and photos of the test results on my personal phone, but I'm not sure if that's even allowed. I joined this company because it had a good reputation, and my father was so proud when I got this job abroad, he told the whole family. I don't want to be the one who comes home in disgrace. But I also became an engineer because I believed that buildings should keep people safe. Some nights I drive past the site and look at the floors going up and feel sick.

I'm 68 and retired from the railways five years ago. My wife and I live in our own house in Varanasi. Our two sons are settled, one in Bangalore and one in Pune, with their own families. For the last few years I have been drawn more and more to spiritual life. I go to the ghats every morning, I read the Gita and the Upanishads, and I have been spending time at an ashram near Rishikesh. Last month the swami there said I could stay permanently if I wished.

I want to. I feel this is what the last part of life is for. But when I told my sons, they were upset. My elder son said I was abandoning their mother and that it was selfish. My younger son said we should sell the house and I should come live with him, so he can look after us. My wife has not said much. She says she will not stop me, but she doesn't want to live alone, and she has never wanted to live in an ashram. She has her friends here, her temple, her routine.

We have enough pension and savings for both of us to live comfortably. My health is good for my age, though I have mild heart trouble. I do not want to hurt my wife, who has been with me forty-two years. But I also feel that if I do not go now, I will die without having done the one thing I truly want.

Is it wrong to leave at this stage? Is there a way to honour my wife and my calling at the same time?

When I was young I wanted to become a sannyasi, but my father needed me to earn, and then I married and the children came, and I did my duty for forty years without complaint. I do not regret that life. But I have always felt that one door was left closed. My wife knows this about me. She once said, half-joking, that she married a man who was always half somewhere else. I do not want her to feel that I am leaving her for something better. I am not. I simply feel the time is short.

I'm a father of two, and my elder daughter, who is 26 and works as an architect in Mumbai, told us last month that she wants to marry a young man from a different caste. He seems decent. He's a software engineer, polite, and from what she says his family is welcoming. My wife cried for two days, not because she dislikes him, but because of what our relatives will say. We live in a small town where everyone knows everyone.

My brothers have already heard. My eldest brother told me that if this marriage happens, he will not attend any family function where they are present. My mother, who is 80, says she wants to see my daughter married before she dies, but 'properly'. My younger daughter, who is 22, is watching all of this closely and I know whatever I do will shape how she thinks about her own life.

I was raised to believe that caste rules keep society in order. I don't fully believe that anymore, I've seen too much of the world. But I'm also afraid of being cut off from my brothers, and of my mother's disappointment. My daughter says she will marry him with or without our blessing, but she wants our blessing. She said 'Papa, I don't want to choose between you and him.'

I love my daughter. I don't want to lose her. I also don't want to lose my family. I don't know if giving my blessing is my duty as a father or a betrayal of my own family. What would you advise?

When my daughter was small, I was the one who told her she could be anything she wanted. I sent her to the best school I could afford, I told her to think for herself. Now she is doing exactly that, and I find I am not as brave as the man who told her those things. My wife says we should at least meet his parents before deciding anything. My daughter has asked if we can do that next month. I have not answered her. Every day I don't answer, I see her hope fading a little more.

so I've been working at this bank for nine years good salary stable everything and for the past two years me and my friend Neha have been building this app on weekends it's a booking tool for small clinics and we have twelve clinics using it now and an investor wants to put in fifty lakhs if both of us go full time by January and I really want to do it like this is the thing I've been dreaming about since college but my wife is five months pregnant our first baby and she's scared she says what if it fails we have a home loan and she's going to take maternity leave and her salary drops and she says just wait two years let the baby come let things settle and I get it I do but the investor won't wait two years and Neha is ready to quit and if I don't she might find another co-founder and I keep thinking if I don't do this now I'll be one of those people who always talks about what they could have done and also my father says a man with a family doesn't gamble and I don't think it's gambling it's a real business with real customers but I also don't want to be the guy who chose his ego over his family we have savings for about eight months if I quit and my wife's parents could help a bit but I don't want to ask them and the thing is I also feel like I'm not fully present at the bank anymore my manager noticed and asked if everything's ok and I said yes but I'm basically working on the app in my head all day and coming home and working on it till one in the morning and my wife says she feels alone in the pregnancy because I'm always on the laptop and she's not wrong and I feel bad about that and maybe if I went full time I could actually be more present at home because I wouldn't be doing two jobs but maybe that's just what I tell myself

Three years ago I lent my closest friend, Imran, four lakhs to save his restaurant. We've been friends since school, our families are close, his mother used to feed me when my own mother was in hospital. He signed nothing, I didn't ask. He promised to repay within a year. He has repaid fifty thousand.

The restaurant is doing better now. I see photos of it full on weekends. He recently bought a new car. When I gently mentioned the money, he said things are still tight and he'll start paying 'soon'. Meanwhile my own situation has changed. My company cut salaries by twenty percent, and I need money for my daughter's admission next year.

My wife is furious. She says he's taking advantage of me and I should tell him clearly or even get a lawyer. My brother says cut him off completely. But Imran is not a bad person, he's careless with money and he probably thinks because we're like brothers I won't really mind. And part of me is ashamed to even bring it up, it feels petty.

I'm also hurt. Not about the money as much as feeling that I matter less to him than his new car. I don't want to lose a friendship of twenty-five years over money. But I also don't want to keep pretending I'm fine and let my family pay for my politeness. How do I handle this?

The worst part is that I have started avoiding him. He invited us to his son's birthday last month and I made an excuse. My wife said I was punishing myself instead of him. Imran even called and asked if he had done something wrong, and I said no, everything's fine, because I didn't know how to start that conversation. Our mothers still talk every week and his mother asked mine whether we had fought. I don't want this to spread to our families. But every time I see that car in his photos, something in me goes cold.

My husband died three years ago in an accident. I was 34. I have two children, a son who is now 12 and a daughter who is 8. For the first two years I just survived. Work, school runs, homework, his parents' visits. My in-laws have been kind in their way, they help with money and pick up the kids sometimes, but they still keep his room in their house the way it was.

Last year I met someone at a parents' meeting at school. His name is Vikram, he's divorced, he has a daughter the same age as mine. We've been seeing each other quietly for eight months. He wants to get married. I think I want to as well. He's good with my children and they like him, although they think he's just a family friend.

My son is the hard part. He was very close to his father, and when another boy at school said something about 'your mother's boyfriend', he came home and screamed at me that I was replacing his papa. I said nothing was happening, which was a lie, and I feel terrible about it.

My mother-in-law has hinted that a widow remarrying 'doesn't look nice', and if I remarry I'm afraid they'll pull away from the children, who love them. My own parents are supportive. I don't know whether to wait until my son is older, or whether waiting is just me being afraid. I also don't want to lose Vikram. Am I being selfish?

Sometimes I go to his grave and talk to him about it. I know he would want me to be happy, he used to say that if anything ever happened to him I shouldn't sit alone. But knowing that doesn't make it easier with my son. My daughter asked me last week if Vikram uncle could come for her birthday, and my son left the room. Vikram says he'll wait as long as needed, but he also says he doesn't want to be a secret forever, and he has his own daughter to think about. She asks him why they can't all be a family.

I've worked at a manufacturing company for eleven years and I'm the most experienced supervisor on my floor. Last month a supervisor post opened at the next level and it went to a man who joined four years after me. I wasn't surprised. Over the years I've heard comments about my caste, never written down, always as 'jokes'. When I first joined, someone left a note on my locker that I won't repeat. I complained then and nothing happened except I was moved to the night shift for six months.

This time I have something different. A friend in HR told me that the promotion committee discussed my 'background' and whether the workers would 'accept' me. She saw the notes. She said she'd deny it if asked, because she'd lose her job.

I have a wife and a son in Class 10, and my salary supports my parents too. If I file a formal complaint, I'll probably be targeted again, and my friend in HR could get into trouble. If I stay quiet, I'll keep doing the work of two people for half the respect, and I'll be teaching my son that this is how life is.

My wife says our son's exams are in four months and we shouldn't create trouble now. My father says he faced worse and survived by keeping quiet. I'm angry, and I'm tired of being told to adjust. I want to stand up for myself and the people who come after me, but I don't want my family to pay for it. What would you do?

I've thought about leaving and joining another company, but I'm 46, and I don't know if I'd find the same pay. My union representative says he'll support a complaint, but he also said, quietly, that management has long memories. There are three younger workers from my community on the floor who look up to me. One of them asked me last week if it's true that people like us never get promoted here. I didn't know what to tell him. I don't want to tell him to give up. But I don't want to give him false hope either.

My husband hits me sometimes. Not every day. Mostly when he has been drinking, maybe once or twice a month. Last week he pushed me against the cupboard and I hit my head. I told the neighbours I fell. We have a daughter who is six. She has seen it twice. The second time she hid under the bed and wouldn't come out for an hour.

I don't have an income. I left my job when she was born because he wanted me to stay home. All the money is in his account and he checks what I spend. My mother says every marriage has problems and I should adjust for the child's sake, that a woman alone with a child has no respect in society. My father died when I was young, and my mother raised me alone, so I don't understand why she says this.

When he's sober he's apologetic, he brings gifts, he plays with our daughter, and I think maybe it will be okay. Then it happens again. I have a friend from college who has offered for us to stay with her in Pune, but I don't know how I'd support us, or what would happen with my daughter's school, or whether he would come after us.

I feel ashamed even writing this. Part of me thinks I'm overreacting because he doesn't do it often. I just want my daughter to grow up happy. What should I do?

I have some gold jewellery from my wedding that is in my name. I've thought about selling it. I've also been looking up how to get a job again, I used to work in accounts. My daughter's school is good and she has friends there, and I don't want to take that away from her. When he is angry he says nobody would want me, that I couldn't survive a week without him. Some days I believe him. Some days I want to prove him wrong. I don't know which of those days to trust.

I'm 16 and in Class 11. My parents want me to do engineering. They've already paid for JEE coaching, it's expensive, my dad took a loan for it. The problem is I don't want to be an engineer. I play the sitar, I've been learning since I was seven, and my guru says I have real talent. There's a music scholarship at a college in Pune that I could apply for, the deadline is in six weeks, and I'd need my parents' signature.

My dad had heart surgery last year and the doctors said he shouldn't have stress. Every time I try to bring up music he gets this look and my mom tells me not to upset him. My mom says music can be a hobby and that musicians don't earn. My older cousin is an engineer in America and everyone compares me to him.

I'm doing badly in coaching. I fail most of the mock tests and I feel stupid there. When I'm playing music I feel like myself. I've started skipping coaching some days and going to my guru's house instead, and my parents don't know. I feel guilty because of the loan and because of my dad's heart.

I don't want to hurt my parents and I don't want to give up music. I'm scared that if I don't apply for the scholarship now, I'll regret it forever, but I'm also scared of what happens if I tell them. What should I do?

My guru has said she will talk to my parents if I want, but I'm scared that will feel like I went behind their backs, which I sort of did. My little brother thinks it's cool that I play sitar and keeps asking me to play for his friends. Sometimes at night I play very softly so my parents don't hear, because my mother says the sound reminds her that I'm not studying. I don't want music to feel like something I have to hide. I just want them to hear me play properly, once, like my guru does.

I'm 15. My parents are getting divorced. They told me and my sister, who is 10, two months ago. My dad is moving to Bangalore for work and my mum is staying here in Chennai. The lawyer said that at my age the court will listen to what I want, so both of them keep asking me who I want to live with.

My dad and I are really close. We play chess, he helps me with maths, and he gets me in a way mum doesn't. But my sister is very close to mum and she's definitely staying with her, and I don't want to be separated from my sister. She's been crying a lot and coming into my room at night. If I go to Bangalore, she'll be alone with mum, and mum has been really sad and not herself.

My school, my friends, my cricket team are all here. But my dad says Bangalore has better schools, and I think he's lonely, he said 'I don't want to lose you too'. My mum hasn't asked me directly, but she keeps saying 'you'll do what's best'. My grandmother told me a son should stay with his mother.

I feel like whatever I say, someone gets hurt. I haven't told my friends anything. I'm finding it hard to concentrate at school and my grades are dropping. I just want someone to tell me what's right.

Last weekend my dad took me to see the flat he's renting in Bangalore. He's already made one room into a room for me, with a desk and a chess board. My mum doesn't know he did that. When I came back, my sister had made me a card that said 'please don't go'. I put it in my drawer. I feel like I'm in the middle of a tug of war and I'm the rope. My class teacher noticed my grades and asked if everything was okay, and I said yes.

ok so I'm 17 and in my friend group everyone has started drinking at parties like on weekends and some of them bunk college to go to this cafe where they smoke and they keep calling me boring because I don't come and last week they made a group without me and I saw the photos and I felt really left out and I don't even want to drink honestly I just want to be with them but my parents are really strict like if they found out I was even at a party where people drink they would take my phone and probably stop me going out at all and my dad is a police officer so it's even worse and I also have my boards in four months and I'm already behind in physics and my best friend Priya used to not drink either but now she does and she says it's not a big deal and I should just try once and I kind of want to just so they stop teasing me but I also don't want to like I feel like I'm changing who I am and I don't know if I'm being a baby or if they're actually not good friends and I don't have anyone else to talk to because my parents would freak out and my sister is in Canada and also I lied to my mom last weekend I said I was at Priya's house studying but actually I went to the party and I didn't drink but I stayed till eleven and I felt really guilty when I came home and my mom asked if I had eaten and I just said yes and went to my room and I don't like lying to her but if I tell her the truth I won't be allowed to go anywhere and then I'll lose my friends for sure so I feel stuck either way and I don't know if this is a normal teenage thing or if I'm making it a big deal

I'm 14 and I don't know who else to tell. A few months ago I started talking to someone online who said he was 16 and went to a school near mine. We talked every day, he was nice, he said I was mature. He asked for photos and I sent some, and then he asked for more private ones and I sent one, which I really regret. Now he's saying that if I don't send more he will post the one I sent and send it to people at my school. He found my school's Instagram and some of my friends.

I'm so scared. I can't sleep and I keep checking my phone. My parents are very traditional and I think if they found out they would be so ashamed of me. My mother always says girls have to protect the family's honour. My older brother would be furious.

I blocked him once but he made a new account and messaged again. He says I have until Saturday. I've thought about just sending more so he stops, but I know that's probably what he wants. I also thought about deleting all my accounts and pretending none of this happened.

There's a teacher at school I trust, she's my class teacher, but I'm scared she'll tell my parents. What do I do?

I've stopped going to my dance class because I'm scared someone there will have seen something. My friends keep asking why I'm so quiet. I keep thinking about what will happen on Saturday. I've read online that some girls in this situation hurt themselves and I don't want to be like that, but I understand now why it happens. I just want this to stop and for nobody to ever know. I feel so stupid for trusting him.

I'm 16 and I've been training in Bharatanatyam for ten years. There's a big competition in three months, the one that can get me a place in a national academy. My teacher says I'm one of her best students but that I need to be 'lighter' to look good on stage. My mother has started saying the same thing and making comments about what I eat in front of the whole family.

So I've been skipping lunch at school and eating very little at dinner, and some days I just have tea. I've lost about five kilos in a month. I feel dizzy sometimes in practice, and last week I nearly fell during a turn. My friends have noticed I don't eat with them anymore. My grandmother keeps putting extra food on my plate and my mother takes it off.

Dance is the most important thing in my life. I want to win this. But I also feel tired all the time, I'm cold even when it's warm, and I can't concentrate in class. Part of me knows this isn't right, and part of me thinks just three more months and then I can eat normally again.

My dad is away working in the Gulf and only calls on weekends. I haven't told him anything. I don't want to disappoint my teacher or my mother, and I don't want to give up the competition. Is it okay to keep going like this until the competition?

My friend Ananya told me her cousin went through something like this and ended up in hospital, and that scared me a bit. But my teacher says every serious dancer does this before a big competition, and that I'll understand when I'm older. I looked at old photos of myself and I don't think I looked heavy, but when I look in the mirror now I still see things I want to change. I don't know who to believe, my teacher, my mother, my friend or myself.
